title: The first scan and a safe start
summary: Use FIRST_SCAN to bring a process into a safe initial state after every start, while production data survives.
objectives: Write startup logic that waits for the operator
Tell which data may resume and which must start safe

sections.heading: Exactly one scan
sections.body: `FIRST_SCAN` is TRUE during the first program scan after each start and FALSE afterwards. STOP, a paused simulation and monitoring do not change it; only an executed scan does. The toolbar shows when a first scan is pending.

sections.heading: A start in time
sections.body: The flag belongs to one scan.
sections.diagram:
STOP ---> start (warm or cold) ---> scan 1 ---> scan 2 ---> scan 3
                                      FIRST_SCAN  FALSE      FALSE
                                      = TRUE

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body: A tank was filling when the PLC restarted. The fill request was retentive, so the inlet opened again by itself. With `IF FIRST_SCAN THEN Filling := FALSE; END_IF;` the inlet stays closed after every start until the operator presses Start; the retentive batch count still survives a warm restart.

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: Making everything non-retentive to get a safe start. The start is safe, but the production data is lost. Decide variable by variable.

sections.heading: Try it
sections.body: Open the safe start exercise and make the startup safe without losing the batch count.

checkpoint.question: The PLC is in STOP for a minute, then set to RUN. In which scan is FIRST_SCAN TRUE?
options: In every scan of the first second
In the first scan after the start only
Never, because STOP to RUN is not a restart
checkpoint.explanation: STOP to RUN is a warm start; FIRST_SCAN is TRUE in its first scan only.

checkpoint.question: Which value should usually not resume after a restart?
options: The number of batches made today
A request to keep a valve open
checkpoint.explanation: An actuator command may be unsafe after the plant has changed; it should wait for the operator.
